arguments: Stateful AEAD operation is not released after successful setup when the handle write-back may fail later at the IPC boundary
message.text: Stateful AEAD operation is not released after successful setup when the handle write-back may fail later at the IPC boundary

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: the finding is supported because AEAD setup allocates an operation, publishes the handle into the output vector before setup, returns success after setup without releasing it, and the IPC wrapper later writes/unmaps output vectors with no cleanup on write-back failure. Evidence: setup validates and stores the handle then allocates at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:104, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:107, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:110, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:111; successful setup falls through to return status at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:154, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:155, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:159, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:259; release is only on the error label at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:261 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_aead.c:263; the caller dispatches then writes/unmaps outputs after the return at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:299, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:301, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:304, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:318, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:320 with no checked rollback before returning at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:327. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Where possible, allocate the operation only after the IPC layer has pinned/validated the destination for the handle, or provide a framework-level cleanup hook that releases newly allocated operations if the final response copy to the client fails. Keep the allocated handle in secure-owned state until successful write-back is guaranteed, or design the handle return path so allocation and handle publication are atomic with respect to IPC failure.
properties.reasoning: The setup path allocates an operation and returns success after psa_aead_*_setup() succeeds, relying on out_vec[0].base to communicate the newly allocated handle to the caller. This file validates only that out_vec[0] is non-NULL and large enough before allocation; it does not include a rollback path for cases where the secure-service return or final write-back to the client fails after the allocation succeeds. In firmware PSA IPC designs, output vectors often cross a privilege boundary, and a client-provided or invalidated output buffer can cause the handle not to be delivered even though the secure partition has consumed an operation slot. If such a late copy/write-back failure is possible in the surrounding framework, repeated setup calls can orphan operation contexts and exhaust the crypto operation pool. This candidate depends on the IPC marshalling semantics outside this file, but the source shows the lifetime coupling between allocation and caller-visible handle delivery without local compensation.
